title: HubSpot cuts nearly 660 jobs as AI reshapes its business
key_facts: HubSpot announced layoffs on Tuesday 6 Oct 2026 of about 660 workers, a 7% staff reduction.
CEO Yamini Rangan wrote the company shifted strategy from helping customers grow to delivering outcomes with AI.
Organisational changes include fewer management layers.
Rangan said the decision is not driven by AI-related efficiencies.
Severance: 20 weeks of base pay plus a week per year of service up to 30 weeks, five months of healthcare and career support.
Q2 revenue rose 20% to nearly $912 million, per the August earnings report.
quote_evidence: HubSpot CEO Yamini Rangan shared the "very difficult news" in a letter to employees that said about 660 workers will be laid off, which amounts to a 7% staff reduction.
She did note that the layoff decision "is not driven by AI-related efficiencies."
why_it_matters_hint: 660 jobs cut, CEO says not AI efficiencies but an AI-focused strategy shift.
notes: CTech page returned no text; read CBS News Boston instead, which quotes the CEO's letter. Other outlets (Boston Globe, Fast Company, Quartz) carry it.
